# Pitex 1.1.2

Closing a local document with unsaved text asks before that text is
discarded. On macOS and Linux, an unchanged preview no longer rewrites
its files.

## Changes

- Closing a tab, choosing Close from the File menu, pressing Command-W,
  clicking the window close button, or quitting asks Save, Don't Save,
  or Cancel when a local document is unsaved or conflicted. Cancel
  leaves the document open. Save writes, then closes. Don't Save closes
  without writing. Escape chooses Cancel.
- On Linux, that question appears before a tab, a project, the window,
  or quit closes an unsaved or conflicted local document. A failed
  switch to another file reports the error and leaves the editor open.
- A remote project still saves on close without this question.
- When the last document is unsaved or conflicted, its close button
  keeps the window on screen until you answer. Quitting with unsaved
  text dismisses the prompt on Cancel and on Escape.
- Commenting a line on the Mac editor uses the text on screen. A
  character you just typed stays, and a range past that text is not
  applied.
- Folding no longer crashes the Mac editor when folded text is shortened
  and the view closes before the fold updates.
- An assistant line longer than 4 MiB is dropped. The next line is kept
  when it is 4 MiB or shorter. Pitex does this on Mac and on Linux.
- On macOS, a fallback build command that contains a NUL byte is
  rejected. Pitex keeps the previous command.
- A folder name that is not UTF-8 no longer quits the preview at
  startup. Opening a second log, xdv, dvi, PDF, or SyncTeX output no
  longer quits it. A PDF predictor with a size below 1, or a row that
  cannot be formed, is skipped. Removing a preview directory that is a
  symlink no longer deletes the folder it points at.
- On macOS and Linux, a preview pass that matches the open publication
  does not write the PDF, the log, or the SyncTeX file again. An edit
  still publishes a new preview. After draft mode, the next finished
  pass publishes once more, so the draft warning can clear. The Windows
  preview helper still writes those files on every pass.
- Windows uninstall removes only the files that installer copied, and it
  removes a directory only when that directory is empty. If this copy of
  Pitex is still running, uninstall asks you to close it and stops.
  Other copies keep running.
- On Windows, opening a file on a volume path opens that file. A path
  that starts with a lowercase UNC prefix opens the server path.
- On Linux, Save As and Save PDF write a temporary file, then replace
  the destination. A failed save does not leave a partial file. A failed
  PDF save shows the error.
- On Linux and Windows, a PDF larger than 50 MiB stays on disk during a
  build. If the build fails, Pitex restores the previous PDF. The build
  log stops at 4 MiB.
- An older transcript reply does not replace the chat on screen. A
  broken Claude tool message does not start the tool.
- On Linux, closing a remote project while the assistant is still
  drawing no longer crashes.

## Install

Pitex 1.0.0 through 1.1.1 update to 1.1.2 from Settings or, with automatic
installation enabled, at launch. For Homebrew installations, run
`brew update` and `brew upgrade --cask pitex`.

Builds from the earlier 2.x line do not update automatically; install 1.1.2
from the downloads below. Pitex Nightly continues to use its separate
update channel.

## Downloads

Downloads include the macOS ARM64 DMG, Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 AMD64 DEBs,
Windows AMD64 installer and portable ZIP, the Ubuntu installer, and
SHA256SUMS.
Windows remains beta.
